test_title: SSC Selection Post Graduation Level Official Paper (Held on: 3 Aug 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Three statements are followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. You have to consider these statements to be true, even if they seem to be at have to consider these statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts. Decide which of the given conclusions logically follow/s from the given statements.

**Statements:**

No bench is a table.

No board is a bench.

Some benches are chalks.

**Conclusions:**

(I) Some chalks are benches.

(II) Some chalks are not tables.

(III) Some chalks are not boards.

options.text: Either conclusion I or conclusion III follows.
Conclusions I, II and III follow

solution:
The least possible Venn Diagram is as follows:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f1e4fb172b82dd4bce293db3f470d79d2b63b9af69ece1097c89081158b3211b.png] 

Conclusions:

(I) Some chalks are benches. → Follows (because some benches are chalks, hence some chalks will definitely be benches.)

(II) Some chalks are not tables. → Follows (because some benches are chalks and no bench is a table, so some chalks are definitely not tables.)

(III) Some chalks are not boards. → Follows (because some benches are chalks and no bench is either a table or a board, so some chalks are definitely not boards.)

Hence, “**Conclusions I, II and III follow**”.
